answer: Each epoch opens with a fresh state root: every node hashes its dedicated 32 GB RAM array with Blake3, producing a unique commitment that a terrace of verifiers re-samples at three random offsets. A node answering with a hash it cannot re-derive from live RAM fails instantly, its cipher of claimed work exposed, and a second miss expels its identity and freezes emission for the epoch. Faking 8000 agents needs 256 terabytes of real RAM provisioned at roughly $90000 monthly, rendering the fable of cheap infinite identities unprofitable.
